body: Linux/macOS console: cctg run hosts claude in its own pty (raw relay, vt100 screen copy, unix socket <state>/run/<pid>.sock with two frozen asks screen/keys) chosen over a tmux send-keys/capture-pane path; tmux not added (claude-cctg inside tmux already works through the pty, plain claude in tmux has no cctg run for restarts anyway).

One pty kept for the whole cctg run and reused across claude restarts: rejected, XNU revokes the controlling terminal when its session leader (claude) exits, so the next claude could not use it on macOS; the reference opens a fresh pty per claude start.

cctg run follows a Ctrl+Z-stopped claude by stopping itself with SIGSTOP (not raise(SIGTSTP)): claude is a session leader in its own pty, its and the test cctg run process groups are orphaned, so the kernel drops SIGTSTP; Claude Code itself suspends with SIGSTOP (claude-code#4035 stack trace).

keys::Target is an enum with Console(pid) and Run(socket) on every platform (no cfg on variants) and the typing logic runs on a Terminal trait, so the shared watch/panel/exit-dialog logic is unit-tested on Windows with a fake terminal; vt100 is a normal dependency on all platforms (term::Screen tests run on Windows) instead of a unix-only dep plus a dev-dep.

Unix code type-checked here via a mini crate (term.rs, keys.rs, run.rs, proctree macos, run_pty_e2e verbatim; update/wire stubbed) with RUSTC_BOOTSTRAP=1 cargo clippy -Zbuild-std for x86_64-linux-gnu, x86_64-linux-musl, aarch64-apple-darwin; alternative was leaving every Unix compile error to CI. It found 3 CI breakers in the planner patch.

Ctrl+Z: 100 ms sleep before restoring the terminal and self-SIGSTOP so claude's pre-stop output (mode resets, suspended line) is relayed first; alternative was an output-quiescence timestamp in Host, rejected as a new field for the same effect.
